newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end lower after choppy session.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end lower after choppy session.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended slightly lower Wednesday, after the U.S. Federal Reserve's beige book found evidence of inflation inconclusive and despite some nervousness about further hostilities in Iraq which helped to firm prices early in the session.
"Precious metals are continuing to consolidate after the declines of the past ten days, though platinum group metals remain weak with Japanese demand soft," Smith Barney analyst David Rinehimer said.
COMEX December gold ended off 20 cents at $386.60 an ounce, after firming early to an session high at $387.70, helped by nervousness about more hostilities in Iraq.
In New York bullion trade, spot gold closed quoted $383.00/383.50, compared to the London afternoon fix at $383.50, and a New York close Tuesday at $383.00-383.40.

After the market closed, U.S. Treasury Secretary Rubin said IMF members were "very close to an agreement" on selling some gold reserves to help finance the IMF's Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility (ESAF) which is designed to alleviate the debt of developing countries.

The IMF board is scheduled to meet Friday to discuss a plan to sell about five million ounces of the IMF's 104 million ounce gold reserve over a period of time, but analysts said the news had probably already been discounted by the market in recent months.
COMEX December silver ended down 0.3 cent at $5.140, after trading in a $5.170-5.100 range.
Both gold and silver drifted lower in the past 10 days on fund selling and weak physical demand by fabricators and investors, ending the July/August rally, analysts said.
NYMEX October platinum ended down $2.60 at $393.10, the lowest level for the October contract since July 8.
NYMEX December palladium closed down 25 cents at $123.70, a new life-of-contract low for December palladium.
Palladium fixed in London Wednesday morning at 33 month low of $123.00 an ounce.
